The Command Center Walkthrough

01

Meet the Command Deck

Open the Command Center and you'll see three zones that never change:

  • Left rail — switch between the Command Deck (your home base), Radar, Partner Schedule, Procedures, and Archive. Your plans list here too, each with a health dot: green is on track, amber has warnings, red needs attention now.
  • Top bar — shows where you are and today's date, plus Export / Import for backups and + New Plan.
  • Main area — whatever view you've picked.

Everything you enter is saved automatically in your browser as you type — there is no Save button anywhere.

Tip Keep this page open as a pinned browser tab. It is designed to sit in the background all day — glance at it, update a task, get back to your email.
02

Create your first plan

Click + New Plan and fill in what you know. Don't stall here — a plan shell with just a name is fine; every field can be added or corrected later with Edit Intake.

  • Plan Type — Startup, Conversion, or Merger (internal/external). This decides which tasks appear: startups skip PRK, Preparation, and Wire Day entirely.
  • Strategy — Cash, Mapping, and/or TIK for conversions and mergers. Strategy-tagged tasks (Re-Registration, TIK Account Details, Liquidate Advanced Employer…) only appear when they apply.
  • Key dates — Case Start (Day 1) drives the Partner Timeline projection; Wire, Effective, and First Payroll @ TA drive countdowns, due dates, and the payroll watch.
  • Characteristics — Loans and Roth add their data-load tasks; the 1/1 flag drops the year-to-date loads that don't apply to January 1 plans.
  • Contacts — payroll vendor and prior record keeper. Leave them blank and the plan carries a visible warning until they're filled in, so nothing slips.
Tip Effective date January 1? The app detects it and treats the plan as a 1/1 plan automatically — the YTD loads disappear from the checklist.
03

Pre-Start: the clock has not started yet

Your new plan opens in Pre-Start. Notice the tasks say "pending — awaiting Obtain All Documents." That's deliberate: due dates are anchored to the day you actually receive the plan documents, so nothing shows as overdue before the engagement has really begun.

Meanwhile the header already works for you:

  • Countdown chips — Wire, Effective, First Payroll, and projected Final Files, each with days remaining. They shift color as dates approach: green → amber (≤10 days) → red (≤3 days).
  • Partner Timeline (right side) — the partner schedule projected onto your real dates: TOA obtained, test file requests, FTP setup, One Payroll approval and more, each snapped to business days.
  • Warnings — missing contacts and other gaps appear as amber banners until resolved.
Heads up Set the Case Start (Day 1) date even if you set nothing else — without it the Partner Timeline stays empty.
04

Start the clock: mark "Obtain All Documents" Done

The single most important click in the whole app. When the PRD/Onboarding package and TOA are in hand, mark Obtain All Documents → Done. Two things happen instantly:

  1. The plan is promoted from Pre-Start to Active.
  2. Every week-anchored task gets a real due window — wk 1 runs from the anchor to that week's Friday, wk 2 is the following Mon–Fri, and so on. Weekend anchors roll forward to Monday, and a task only turns red once its bucket has fully passed.

Wire-day and post-wire tasks calculate separately from your Wire date in business days — weekends and federal holidays are skipped, matching the partner schedule exactly.

Tip Un-checking Obtain All Documents moves the plan back to Pre-Start and returns tasks to pending. Nothing is lost — the clock just stops.
05

Work the phases

Each phase is a card — Setup, Payroll, PRK, Preparation, Wire Day, Post Wire, Data Load, Closeout — showing only the tasks that apply to this plan's type and strategy. Every task has four states:

  • OPEN — not started. WKG — in progress. DONE — finished (struck through, drops out of every triage list). N/A — doesn't apply (grayed, excluded from progress counts).

Click a status a second time to toggle back to Open. Critical tasks like Obtain All Documents, Payroll Handoff, and the Go-Live Meeting have no N/A — they must actually happen.

Hit + note under any task for a quick context line — "waiting on their spec sheet, promised by Wed." Future-you will thank you. Phase headers collapse when you click them, and fully-done phases fold up on their own.

06

Add your own tasks

Real plans always grow extra to-dos the checklist didn't predict. Every phase card ends with + Add task: type the name, optionally pick a due date, press Enter or click Add.

Custom tasks get a CUSTOM badge and a Remove control, and otherwise behave identically: they count toward progress, take statuses and notes, and show up in Overdue / This Week / Radar when dated. They survive export and import along with everything else.

07

Pin a due date when reality disagrees

The generated schedule is a model — reality sometimes disagrees. Click the small ✎ pencil next to any task's due date to pin your own date. Pinned dates show as "due Jul 24 · pinned" and always win over the calculated one. Clear the pin any time to fall back to the model.

Pins on the two anchor tasks are extra powerful: pin a date on Obtain All Documents or Receive Final Files and every downstream forecast re-flows from it — useful when you know documents will land next Tuesday and want the projected schedule now.

08

Triage from the Deck — your daily habit

With plans in flight, the Deck becomes your morning ritual. Top to bottom:

  • KPI band — active plans, overdue count, due-this-week count, payroll watch, and the next wire date. Red and amber numbers are your cue.
  • Overdue / This Week / Payroll Watch panels — actual tasks across all plans, worst first. Click any row to jump straight to that plan. When a list is long you'll see "+N more — view all in Radar."
  • Plan cards — date chips with countdowns, progress bar, and any warnings. Open, Edit, or put a plan on Hold right from the card.

Payroll Watch deserves respect: it fires when a plan's first payroll is within 14 days and Payroll Handoff isn't done — the single most expensive thing to miss in a conversion. It goes red inside 7 days.

Tip The red badge on "Radar" in the left rail is your total overdue count — visible from every view, so nothing hides.
09

Radar: everything dated, day by day

The Deck answers "what needs me today?" — Radar answers "what's coming?" Every dated task on every active plan, grouped by day, overdue items pinned to the top. Use the plan filter to focus on a single case before a status call.

10

Partner Schedule: the reference card

When a client asks "when should payroll have their specs back?", this is your answer sheet: the full partner schedule with each milestone's anchor (D1 case start, EFF effective date, WIRE wire date) and business-day offset. TIK-only and merger-only rows are tagged. The same offsets power each plan's Partner Timeline sidebar, so the reference and your plans can never disagree.

The Procedures view sits next door — step-by-step pages for Census, Elections, Source Mapping, Fund Mapping and the three balance-import strategies, one click away when you're in the weeds.

11

Wire day, final files, and the data loads

On wire day, knock down the Wire Day card: morning emails, receive the wire, then move it — the third task adapts to your strategy (Transfer to Advanced Employer for cash, Map Funds for mapping; TIK-only plans skip it).

Post-wire, everything hinges on one event: Receive Final Files → Done. Until then the data loads sit pending; the moment you mark it, Census, Elections, Deferrals, Eligibility and the rest all get concrete dates — seven business days out, with Final Check trailing. One click, and the last mile schedules itself.

12

Closeout: the plan archives itself

There's no "mark complete" button, because completion is defined by the work: when Go-Live Meeting Complete and Payroll Handoff / Finalize are both Done, the plan flips to Complete and moves to the Archive on its own. Your deck stays clean — only live work in view.

Archived plans keep their full history. Reopen one if go-live turns out to be less final than advertised, or use Archive / Hold from any plan header to park work manually.

13

Make it yours: theme, backups, and where your data lives

Last things worth knowing:

  • Theme — the ◐ button in the bottom-left flips light/dark; it follows your system preference until you choose. The layout adapts down to phone width.
  • Your data lives in this browser — plans are stored locally, private to your machine. That means: use Export regularly. It downloads a JSON snapshot of every plan.
  • Import — restoring or moving to a new machine, Import asks before touching anything: merge (updates matching plans, adds new ones, keeps the rest) or replace all, which demands a second explicit confirmation. A malformed file is rejected without changing a thing.
Heads up Clearing your browser data clears your plans. Export a backup at the end of each week — it takes one click.
★

Quick reference

The daily loop

  1. Open the Deck — scan the KPI band.
  2. Clear the Overdue panel first, then This Week.
  3. Respect the Payroll Watch. Always.
  4. Mark work Done as it happens; add notes for anything in flight.

Moments that matter

  • Docs arrive → mark Obtain All Documents — starts every clock.
  • Final files arrive → mark Receive Final Files — schedules all data loads.
  • Go-Live + Payroll Handoff done → plan archives itself.

Statuses

  • OPEN — queued  ·  WKG — in progress
  • DONE — finished, leaves all lists
  • N/A — doesn't apply, excluded from counts
  • Click a status again to undo it.

Why does it say…

  • "pending — awaiting…" → the anchor task isn't done yet; no false overdues.
  • "wk 2: Jul 27 – Jul 31" → a week bucket; red only after Friday passes.
  • "due Aug 3 · pinned" → someone pinned it; the pencil clears it.
